model.name: H.R. 2317 (119th)
model.title: Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2026

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2025
This bill provides for the designation, conveyance, exchange, sale, or disposal of certain federal lands in Nevada.

Specifically, the bill provides for the transfer of ownership of federal lands from the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management to the State of Nevada, counties (Douglas, Clark, Pershing, and Elko Counties), cities (Carson City, City of Elko, the City of Fernley, and the City of Sparks), the Incline Village General Improvement District, and the Truckee River Flood Management Authority for economic development, recreation, or certain public purposes.
It also designates specified parcels of federal land as wilderness and as components of the National Wilderness Preservation System.
The bill also releases the reversionary interest of the United States in the Jean Prison site, thereby allowing the State of Nevada to use the land for purposes unrelated to the prison.

It also allows the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to establish a federal complex for specified Bureau of Land Management, Forest Service, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Reclamation, and Bureau of Indian Affairs offices or headquarters in Nevada on certain federal lands.
Additionally, the bill takes land into trust for the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California.

This bill would move ownership of certain federal lands in Nevada to state and local governments and other public bodies, mainly for economic development, recreation, or other public purposes. The land would come from the Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management and would go to the State of Nevada; Douglas, Clark, Pershing, and Elko Counties; Carson City, the City of Elko, the City of Fernley, and the City of Sparks; the Incline Village General Improvement District; and the Truckee River Flood Management Authority.
The bill would also set aside specific federal land parcels as wilderness, adding them to the National Wilderness Preservation System.
In addition, the United States would give up its reversionary interest in the Jean Prison site. This means the State of Nevada could use that land for purposes other than a prison.

The bill would allow the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to set up a federal complex in Nevada on certain federal lands. The complex could house offices or headquarters for the Bureau of Land Management, the Forest Service, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the Bureau of Reclamation, and the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
Finally, the bill would take certain land into trust for the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California.
